issues.description: The solution declares Bookstore.books as a private property, but Client.main (in a different source file) accesses bookstore.books to print the inventory. In Swift, a 'private' member is limited to the declaring source file, so the Client's access will not compile. The problem statement and example expect Client to iterate over the bookstore's books.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the books collection accessible to Client. Options: (1) Remove the 'private' modifier so it's internal (e.g. 'let books: [Book]'), (2) expose a read-only public/internal accessor (e.g. 'public var books: [Book] { self._books }' with a private backing store), or (3) add a public method on Bookstore to iterate or provide the inventory. Any of these will allow Client.main to access the books and will preserve the intended design.
